solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Note queen occupying house, say

indicators.note: to occupy a house is to live inside it, so one piece sits within the others

parts.note: a semi is a semi-detached house, a common British home
QU is a standard abbreviation for queen
to aver is to state or say firmly

explanation.surface: A message that a queen is staying in some house or other.
explanation.walkthrough: 'house, say' reads as one phrase, an example of a house, but 'say' is a separate piece; a semi is a semi-detached British house.
explanation.definitionFit: A semiquaver is a sixteenth note in music, half the length of a quaver.

clue.text: Amount added to account? It may bear fruit

parts.note: a sum is an amount
AC is the abbreviation for account

explanation.surface: Money paid into a bank account that may earn interest, bearing fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bear fruit' sounds like an investment paying off, but it is a literal plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Sumac is a shrub or small tree whose clusters of red berries are dried as a spice.

clue.text: Decorative veneer sample with leading brand

indicators.note: the leading item goes in front of the other

parts.note: a marque is a brand, especially of car
to sample something is to try it

explanation.surface: A sample of decorative wood finish offered alongside a top brand.
explanation.definitionFit: Marquetry is inlaid work of shaped wood pieces applied as a pattern on furniture surfaces.

clue.text: Put up with one hammering meat

parts.note: to quarter troops is to put them up, lodge them
someone who pounds is hammering away

explanation.surface: Tolerating a person who keeps hammering at a piece of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Put up with' looks like 'tolerate', but 'Put up' is lodge and 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A quarter-pounder is a burger patty weighing a quarter of a pound of beef.

clue.text: Maybe music class getting answer right at first

indicators.note: what comes at first is placed at the front of the other letters

parts.note: A is the abbreviation for answer
RT is an abbreviation for right
a form is a school class in Britain

explanation.surface: A music class where a pupil gets the right answer first time.
explanation.definitionFit: An art form is a recognised medium of creative expression, and music is one example.

clue.text: Corrode a metal in periodically scratched section

indicators.note: the first pieces go inside the remaining letters
letters scratched out at regular intervals leave every other one

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of section
tin is a metal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Rust appearing in a scratched section of metal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scratched' looks like damage to the metal, but with 'periodically' it tells you to strike out every other letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat into something is to wear it away gradually, as rust or acid does.

clue.text: Love last of chess captures winning back piece

indicators.note: to capture is to take in and hold, so the outer letters surround the rest

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, shaped like the letter O

indicators.note: going back means the word for winning is read from right to left

parts.note: a side that is winning is up, as in one up

indicators.note: the last of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of chess

explanation.surface: A chess lover's commentary on a final capture that wins back material.
explanation.walkthrough: The chess surface makes 'piece' look like a chessman, but it is a piece of music or writing.
explanation.definitionFit: An opus is a musical or literary work, and a piece is just such a composition.

clue.text: Aide saving regular tranches of venture capital once

indicators.note: to save something is to keep it safe inside

parts.note: a PA, personal assistant, is an aide

indicators.note: taking slices at regular intervals means picking every other letter

parts.note: the second, fourth and sixth letters of venture

explanation.surface: An assistant setting aside slices of venture capital funding.
explanation.walkthrough: 'venture capital' reads as a finance term, but capital is the definition, qualified by 'once'.
explanation.definitionFit: Petra, in modern Jordan, was the ancient capital city of the Nabataean kingdom.

clue.text: Start to scarper, fly, go off and leg it

indicators.note: the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of scarper
a ked is a wingless parasitic fly found on sheep
eggs that addle go bad, or go off

explanation.surface: A string of words for running away: scarper, fly, go off, leg it.
explanation.walkthrough: Every word looks like another synonym for fleeing; only the last is the definition. Scarper and leg it are British slang for run off.
explanation.definitionFit: To skedaddle is to run away hurriedly, just as to leg it is to flee.

clue.text: What witches do with e.g. worker's legal agreement

parts.note: a coven is a gathering of witches, and what it does is its deed
a worker is an example of an ant, the caste that forages

explanation.surface: A legal contract mixing witches' activities with labour rights.
explanation.definitionFit: A deed of covenant is a formal legal document binding someone to regular payments, once used for UK charity giving.

clue.text: Cutting time on ring road fellow circles

indicators.note: placed on, in an across answer, means added after the other letters
to circle something is to go right round it, so one piece surrounds the others

parts.note: a fellow is a man
a ring is round, like the letter O
RD is the abbreviation for road
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: A traveller saving time by taking a ring road that some man drives round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ring road' reads as one thing, but ring and road are separate pieces, and 'on' puts time at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Mordant wit is sharp and biting, so cutting is a direct synonym for this adjective.

clue.text: On vacation, amusement in that place in play area?

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: there means in that place

indicators.note: a word on vacation is emptied out, leaving only its outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of amusement

explanation.surface: A holidaymaker looking for fun where the children can play.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a 'play area' is a playhouse, not a playground.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre is the place where plays are staged, punningly described as an area for play.

clue.text: Procession of figures not unknown in part of Ireland

indicators.note: saying something is not there means taking it out

parts.note: County Down is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland
in algebra x, y and z are unknowns

explanation.surface: A parade of people marching somewhere in the Irish countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the unknown Y from COUNTY DOWN leaves COUNTDOWN. 'Figures' suggests people, but it means numbers.
explanation.definitionFit: A countdown is a sequence of numbers called out in turn, such as before a rocket launch.

clue.text: Short introduction to Armenian song and dance

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of spirits, a 'short' in British pub talk

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its opening letter

parts.note: the first letter of Armenian

explanation.surface: A brief preview of an Armenian folk performance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Short' looks like an adjective modifying introduction, but it is a noun: a short is a small drink of spirits. Readers may know the dram as Armenia's currency, which adds to the trap.
explanation.definitionFit: Making a song and dance is making a big fuss, which is what a drama is.

clue.text: Drive, coming out of Malmo, to Riga

indicators.note: the letters emerge from inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: the run straddles the end of Malmo, the word to and the start of Riga

explanation.surface: A road trip from Sweden's Malmo to the Latvian capital Riga.
explanation.definitionFit: To motor is to travel by car, so it means to drive as a verb.

clue.text: Old lady's looking sad, abandoned by a virtuoso

parts.note: an old lady is slang for one's mother, ma

indicators.note: if something is abandoned by a letter, that letter leaves it

parts.note: looking sad and close to tears
taken as written

explanation.surface: A mother left tearful because a gifted performer has walked out on her.
explanation.walkthrough: MA'S TEARFUL loses its A to become MASTERFUL.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuoso as an adjective means showing great skill, like a masterly or masterful performance.

clue.text: Low Head of News turned to round of features

parts.note: to low is to make the sound a cow makes

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

parts.note: the first letter of News
to turn to something is to face it

explanation.surface: A depressed editor in charge of the news turning to someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low' and 'Head of News' sound like a gloomy boss, but low is the cow's call.
explanation.definitionFit: Moon-faced describes a person with a round, full face, so the features are round.

clue.text: Strong drink stirred reaction, you heard

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so the letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: what is heard is a sound, so the word is replaced by a letter that sounds the same

parts.note: the letter U is said the same as the word you

explanation.surface: Someone describing how a stiff drink stirred a reaction in you.
explanation.definitionFit: Cointreau is a French orange liqueur, around 40 percent alcohol.

clue.text: Increase in sweet food taken into kind of blue movie

indicators.note: something taken into another thing ends up inside it

parts.note: sky blue is a shade of blue
rock is a hard stick of candy sold at British seaside towns
E.T. is the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: Someone eating more sweets while watching a sad or racy film.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blue movie' suggests an adult film, but blue belongs to its own phrase and the movie is Spielberg's alien.
explanation.definitionFit: To skyrocket is to rise steeply and suddenly, as prices do, so it means increase as a verb.

clue.text: A thousand I withheld from lousier clothes-maker?

parts.note: K stands for a thousand

indicators.note: something withheld from a word is held back, taken out of it

parts.note: lousier in the literal sense: having more lice and nits
taken as written

explanation.surface: A shoddy garment maker being paid a thousand less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lousier' looks like 'worse', but here it means more infested with nits; take one I out.
explanation.definitionFit: A knitter makes jumpers and scarves from yarn, so is literally a maker of clothes.

clue.text: Hosting East German, bit a kind of pancake

indicators.note: a host holds guests inside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: a tad is a small bit
Ost is the German word for east
taken as written

explanation.surface: An East German guest biting into a pancake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'East German' suggests the old GDR, but it means the German word for east.
explanation.definitionFit: A tostada is a Mexican flat tortilla fried until crisp, loosely a kind of pancake.

clue.text: Delayed expression of approval?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: put aside for later, postponed
second meaning: read as two words, an exclamation of 'Oh, nice!'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests praise given late; the question mark warns that the second meaning splits the phrase into O and NICE.
explanation.definitionFit: A plan put on ice is shelved for later, and 'O nice' is a pleased exclamation of approval.

clue.text: East to west, head for German city

indicators.note: in an across answer, heading west means running right to left, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: a ness is a headland, as in Loch Ness's shore names and Inverness
E is the abbreviation for east

explanation.surface: Travel directions from east to west, heading for a city in Germany.
explanation.walkthrough: NESS followed by E, then turned to run westwards, gives ESSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: Essen is an industrial city in Germany's Ruhr region.

clue.text: Feel this could make 21

indicators.note: the answer's letters could be made into another word by rearranging them

parts.note: the answer to 21 across

explanation.surface: A hint that a feeling could produce the answer to another clue.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue works backwards: rearranging the answer gives 21's ESSEN, so the same letters rearranged give SENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: To sense something is to perceive or feel it.

clue.text: Examiner not precise in translation out of English

indicators.note: a translation renders words differently, so the letters are rearranged
out of English means with the abbreviation for English removed

parts.note: taken as written
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A marker complaining that a translation from English is inaccurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not precise' looks like a description of the examiner, but it is the raw letters: drop one E, then rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: An inspector examines things officially, such as schools, tickets or crime scenes.

clue.text: Concerned with politician concealing a plot again

parts.note: re means concerning, about

indicators.note: something concealing another hides it within

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament
taken as written

explanation.surface: A worried politician hiding a conspiracy that is being hatched again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'plot' suggests a scheme, but here it means to plot on a map.
explanation.definitionFit: To remap is to chart or map an area once more, plotting it again.

clue.text: Nab criminal wearing soft fabric, one running the cooler

indicators.note: the word for fabric is worn around the other letters, enclosing them

parts.note: felt is a soft matted cloth

indicators.note: something criminal is crooked, so the letters are bent out of order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Arresting a crook in soft clothing who is running a prison, the cooler.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cooler' is slang for jail, so the surface reads as police work; the cooler is really the car radiator.
explanation.definitionFit: A fan belt drives the engine's cooling fan in a car, so it keeps the radiator cooling system running.

clue.text: Somewhere in California I see in Maine, surprisingly?

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the state name
a surprising result is unexpected, so the letters come out in an unexpected order

parts.note: taken as written
ah is what you say when you understand: I see

explanation.surface: Someone surprised to see a California place turn up in the state of Maine.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaheim is a city in Orange County, California, home of Disneyland.

clue.text: In France the art remains shunned by consumers

parts.note: le is French for the
in French tu es means thou art

explanation.surface: French art left unbought by a public that ignores it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In France' applies to both words: the French for 'the' and for 'art' as in 'thou art', not art as painting.
explanation.definitionFit: Lees are the dregs left in the bottle or cask, the sediment drinkers leave behind.

clue.text: Animal trainer securing right means to get milk

indicators.note: to secure something is to hold it fast within

parts.note: a beast is an animal
R is the abbreviation for right
a pump is a light canvas shoe, like a trainer, in British usage

explanation.surface: A circus animal trainer getting the right to milk something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Animal trainer' reads as one person, but trainer is the sneaker-type shoe; BEAST holds R, followed by PUMP.
explanation.definitionFit: A breast pump is a device nursing mothers use to express milk.
